correctness.rationale: For d>=2, genus and conic Bezout give D^2>=d-2, establishing completeness of negative curves. Exact intersections imply selected (-1)-curves are disjoint, secant edges pairwise intersect, and the conic block is negative definite iff the selected E count is <n-4. Edge families are precisely stars and triangles, yielding both binomial polynomials. -K=H+Q is big, so the Bauer--Schmitz volume dichotomy gives finite vs infinite exactly by conic support. Exact standalone edge-backtracking checks m<=11, geometric support comparisons n=7..10, full rational matrix definiteness at n=7, and total formula through n=19 were replayed with ALL_CHECKS_PASSED. Finite computation does not replace symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: Specific original assessed statement: closed support-size polynomials and total/finite/infinite chamber counts uniformly for n>=7 conic-point plane blowups. Bauer--Funke--Neumann provides a general algorithm and the support correspondence, and Bauer--Schmitz supplies the volume criterion, but neither inspected full text has the conic-family enumeration. Restricting the formula to n=6 would not imply the n>=7 classification without the new genus/Bézout negative-curve proof and arbitrary-n star/triangle enumeration. Targeted exact-sequence, title, and equivalent-statement searches did not find an exact counterpart. Historical priority remains a risk.
residual_risks: A specialist thesis or table may implicitly or explicitly tabulate the n>=7 conic-point chamber count despite its absence from the searched results.

value.rationale: An exact support-size and volume-finiteness census for every n>=7 within a natural classical geometric family is a natural stable-base-locus invariant, not a chosen arbitrary slice. The persistence of finitely many chambers for unbounded n sharply contrasts with generic n>=9 blowups, and the all-n result requires a nontrivial negative-curve elimination plus Schur-complement and intersecting-edge enumeration. Its finite/infinite support split gives more structure than a lone count or a routine n=7 increment.
